claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can process composite powders containing RHEA components and Cu.
SPS provides rapid reaction conditions in RHEA-Cu composite powders.
Rapid SPS conditions favor the formation of stable, fine-scale interfacial phases.
The interfacial phases formed during SPS mitigate difficulties arising from the positive heat of mixing between Cu and refractory alloying elements.
High-temperature, high-pressure SPS under an inert atmosphere induces rapid reaction and controlled solid-state diffusion.
Short sintering durations minimize excessive diffusion and phase segregation during large-scale processing.
SPS forms thin, stable interfacial phases at RHEA-Cu boundaries.
The interfacial phases act as diffusion barriers.
The interfacial phases inhibit grain growth.
Rapid heating and short dwell times during SPS promote a reaction-synthesized microstructure.
Controlled interdiffusion during SPS forms interfacial phases that compensate for thermodynamic immiscibility between Cu and RHEA elements.
Formation of the interfacial phases produces a more uniform and stable RHEA-Cu composite microstructure.
SPS-processed RHEA-Cu composites will have a more refined and stable microstructure than conventionally sintered composites.
SPS-processed RHEA-Cu composites will exhibit better mechanical performance than conventionally sintered composites.
SPS-processed RHEA-Cu composites will exhibit better irradiation resistance than conventionally sintered composites.
Conventional sintering often produces significant elemental segregation and unstable microstructures because of the positive mixing enthalpy between Cu and refractory elements.
Unoptimized SPS temperature, pressure, or dwell time can prevent formation of the proposed stable microstructure.
Temperature gradients introduced during scale-up can cause nonuniform reaction kinetics.
No direct cited evidence links SPS parameters to mitigation of positive-heat-of-mixing effects in RHEA-Cu composites.
